summary: Radar for 2026-11-08 (GLP-1 focus). The best early catch is the full retatrutide knee osteoarthritis Phase 3 data. It was presented at ACR today (Nov 8) and medicalxpress reports it as published in NEJM. That gives us the 'new Phase 3 data / what's confirmed' Short the playbook asks for. Creators haven't covered it yet; only science press and NewsBytes have. Before anyone uses the numbers, check the size and dose figures against the NEJM paper. Medicalxpress says 'more than 1,000 combined' and 'about 25%'. The December topline said 445 people in TRIUMPH-4 and up to 28.7%. Three practical tirzepatide questions have new hooks this week. (1) 'Skin hurts to touch' (allodynia) got mainstream pickup from NewsNation on Nov 6. It fits next to the injection-site long-form, which is now 12 snapshots in a row at momentum 87. (2) A new cohort study on starting NSAIDs and GI bleeding in GLP-1 users (AJHP, Nov 5) opens a Lane A question nobody has answered: 'Can I take ibuprofen on tirzepatide?' (3) Medscape's 'Keeping the weight off after stopping' (Nov 7) is a ready funnel to the stopping long-form. Thanksgiving is accelerating ahead of the Nov 18–27 peak, so pen storage for travel and alcohol/drinking-less angles ride along with it. ObesityWeek (Nov 14–17) is the next big event: REDEFINE 4, CagriSema vs tirzepatide, the only kind of news that could earn an L2 long-form. Retatrutide gray-market coverage is surging (MedPage, Sky News, MHRA). That's fine for one safety-framed Short this week, never sourcing. Rejected: Lilly–Hims direct sales, insurance coverage cuts, the Medicaid/Medicare $50 bridge and online platforms (cost and pharmacy are banned), plus the CFL 'presented by Wegovy' noise. I couldn't open two PubMed abstracts, the NSAID and alcohol studies: they hit a cookie wall. The scriptwriter has to pull their exact numbers before any script goes out.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide for knee osteoarthritis pain: full TRIUMPH-4 and TRIUMPH-1-OA Phase 3 results (ACR 2026, Nov 8; reported in NEJM)
candidates.angle: 'Retatrutide knee pain: what's confirmed?' Two Phase 3 trials in adults with overweight/obesity and knee OA, compared with placebo. Medicalxpress reports about two-thirds on retatrutide had at least a 50% drop in knee pain vs 38% on placebo, and about 25% average weight loss at the highest dose. Say it's still investigational and not approved, and that online 'research' products aren't the trial drug. Use a loop ending.
candidates.why_now: Full peer-reviewed Phase 3 data came out today at ACR, with same-day pickup from medicalxpress, New Atlas and NewsBytes. Retatrutide Shorts with new Phase 3 data are a playbook-approved 13:00 lead (T2D Short 279 views). Mainstream health creators haven't caught up yet. Before scripting, verify n (445 in TRIUMPH-4), each dose arm and the estimand against the NEJM paper.

evidence.signal: Two Phase 3 trials; about two-thirds had at least a 50% knee-pain reduction vs 38% on placebo; NEJM + ACR
TRIUMPH-4 trial record (overweight/obesity + knee OA)
Topline: 445 adults, 9 mg/12 mg vs placebo, 68 weeks, up to 28.7% weight loss, WOMAC pain −4.0/−3.7 vs −2.1

candidates.topic: 'My skin hurts to touch' on a GLP-1 medicine: allodynia (painful skin sensitivity), now in mainstream news
candidates.angle: An 08:00 body-worry Short: 'Tirzepatide and skin that hurts to touch: is this normal?' Be honest. The published reports so far are a small semaglutide case series (4 patients, after dose increases, reported as temporary) plus pharmacovigilance signals, and nobody has shown that tirzepatide causes it. Give one new fact, and say when to tell your prescriber. Never upgrade 'reports of' to a confirmed rate.
candidates.why_now: NewsNation ran it on Nov 6, after the Daily Beast's earlier pickup. It's a scary-sounding new side effect people will search right away, and few calm, evidence-graded answers exist. It sits right next to the injection-site long-form, so it works as a funnel.

candidates.topic: Keeping weight off after stopping tirzepatide: Medscape (Nov 7), plus SURMOUNT-4 and US real-world data showing regain isn't the same for everyone
candidates.angle: A 20:00 funnel Short to the stopping long-form: 'If I stop tirzepatide, will all the weight come back?' SURMOUNT-4: on placebo after week 36, 14.0% regain to week 88, but still 9.9% below starting weight on average. Real-world: about 36% kept weight off and 36% kept losing at 18 months (observational, semaglutide or tirzepatide). Say it before any tip: don't stop or change your medicines on your own.
